entries.speaker: converge
entries.heard: >> YOU NEED TO GET INTO THIS RECORD. IT'S huge huge influence on both of us. This was a game-changing record for me.
entries.quote: You need to get into this record. It's a huge, huge influence on both of us. This was a game-changing record for me.
entries.citation: Converge, on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, say of NoMeansNo's Wrong: "It's a huge, huge influence on both of us. This was a game-changing record for me."
entries.note: Both guests are on camera; "both of us" covers both, so it speaks for the band.

entries.speaker: converge
entries.heard: >> I [ __ ] listen to this record all the time still, and every single time I'm like, how the [ __ ] did they do this in 1974? Like, how?
entries.quote: I [bleep] listen to this record all the time still, and every single time I'm like, how the [bleep] did they do this in 1974? Like, how?
entries.note: Admiration from a distance; no tie to their own music. Speaker could be either member.

entries.speaker: bikini-kill
entries.heard: I'm still mad but um I love VOR in all her incarnations um I love a lot of the
entries.quote: I'm still mad but, um, I love Björk in all her incarnations.
entries.note: Captions say "VOR"; the passage (Sugarcubes cassette, a woman credited less than her male producers) is Björk. The cassette is the Sugarcubes' Life's Too Good. A fan, nothing about her own music.

entries.speaker: sparks
entries.heard: She's super. Again, an artist that created their own kind of universe and and and style. And I I've always relate so much to vocalists especially that
entries.quote: She's super. Again, an artist that created their own kind of universe and style. And I've always related so much to vocalists, especially that
entries.note: Admires her as a vocalist with her own style; nothing about shaping Sparks.

entries.speaker: fontaines-dc
entries.heard: that's yeah so next one is one of my favorite bands ever this is broadcast
entries.quote: So next one is one of my favorite bands ever. This is Broadcast.
entries.note: Speaker could be either guest. Fandom with no tie to Fontaines' own music.

entries.speaker: fontaines-dc
entries.heard: the boys so I have uh Pixies here um do little which is just like a really important album to me for Bas playing and back and vocals and stuff like I'm
entries.quote: So I have Pixies here. Doolittle, which is just like a really important album to me for bass playing and backing vocals and stuff.
entries.citation: A member of Fontaines D.C., on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, says of the Pixies' Doolittle: "It's a really important album to me for bass playing and backing vocals."
entries.note: Captions: "Bas playing and back and vocals". Which of the two guests speaks is not clear; the bass playing points to the band's bassist. Tied to his own playing, so counted as influence.

entries.speaker: gang-of-four
entries.record: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars
entries.heard: growing up so then the record that changed my life our lives many of us that just did it took us into a whole new world
entries.quote: ...growing up. So then the record that changed my life, our lives, many of us, that just took us into a whole new world.
entries.citation: Hugo Burnham of Gang of Four, on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, says of Bowie's Ziggy Stardust: "The record that changed my life, our lives, many of us... took us into a whole new world."
entries.note: The record is identified from what follows (Haddon Street sleeve, "Starman" on Top of the Pops in 1972), not from a named title. 1972 is before the band formed.

entries.speaker: magdalena-bay
entries.speakerName: Magdalena Bay (Mica Tenenbaum or Matthew Lewin)
entries.heard: So yeah, I feel like I'm a big REMM fan, but my knowledge of it is like Murmur and then I kind of skip forward to like
entries.quote: So yeah, I feel like I'm a big R.E.M. fan, but my knowledge of it is like Murmur and then I kind of skip forward to Out of Time and then onwards.
entries.note: Says they have not explored the early records; fandom from a distance. Speaker is one of the two guests, not clear which.

entries.speaker: magdalena-bay
entries.speakerName: Magdalena Bay (Mica Tenenbaum or Matthew Lewin)
entries.heard: Prague classic, King Crimson's Red. I was looking for Discipline, but I didn't find it just because like that's what I've been listening to lately. But
entries.quote: Prog classic, King Crimson's Red. I was looking for Discipline, but I didn't find it, just because that's what I've been listening to lately.
entries.note: Came to them recently; no link to their own music. Speaker is one of the two guests.

entries.speaker: snail-mail

entries.quote: ...the statue that they had on stage during that tour, just as like extreme inspiration for stage production.
entries.note: Inspiration for stage production (a t-shirt and the In Utero tour statue), not for her songwriting; kept as favourite to be strict.

entries.speaker: snail-mail
entries.heard: this is my favorite elliot smith record it was one of those things where uh i was like do i go with a record that i've
entries.quote: This is my favorite Elliott Smith record.
entries.note: Praise only.

entries.speaker: snail-mail
entries.heard: the score is insane um i'm a huge sufjan stevens fan
entries.quote: The score is insane. I'm a huge Sufjan Stevens fan.
entries.note: Fan of the soundtrack songs; nothing about her own music.

entries.speaker: tame-impala
entries.heard: of like taught me that band music can feel like electronic music. To me, these guys were like electronic music before electronic music started. It was like
entries.quote: These guys kind of like taught me that band music can feel like electronic music. To me, these guys were like electronic music before electronic music started.
entries.citation: Kevin Parker of Tame Impala, on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, says of Can: "These guys kind of like taught me that band music can feel like electronic music."
entries.note: Pick is a Can t-shirt and Future Days; he goes on to say it was part of making music that fused organic band music with electronic music.

entries.speaker: tame-impala
entries.heard: fan of music, but was obsessed with this album. I had been into a lot of new metal and stuff from like when I was a kid. Deaf Tones was the one that like
entries.quote: ...fan of music, but was obsessed with this album. I had been into a lot of nu metal and stuff from when I was a kid.
entries.note: Borderline: obsessed with it in his teens ("carried through into teenage years"), framed as nostalgia, nothing about his own music. Kept favourite to be strict.

entries.speaker: talking-heads
entries.record: Joy as an Act of Resistance
entries.heard: magazines and reviews and things like this. It's highly recommended, but I thought, "Oh, let's have a serious listen to it.
entries.quote: ...magazines and reviews and things like this. It's highly recommended, but I thought, "Oh, let's have a serious listen to it."
entries.note: A staff pick he had not heard; the "Britain's most necessary band" line is the shop sticker read aloud. Curiosity, not influence.

entries.speaker: interpol
entries.heard: D.C. is sort of a hub for hardcore music and stuff like that and I was kind of weaned on that and being around that. This is the record that really reeled me in and to this day I think it's one of the best hardcore records ever and I'll never tire of it.
entries.quote: D.C. is sort of a hub for hardcore music and stuff like that, and I was kind of weaned on that and being around that. This is the record that really reeled me in.
entries.citation: A member of Interpol, on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, says of Bad Brains' ROIR Sessions: "I was kind of weaned on that and being around that. This is the record that really reeled me in."
entries.note: Captions are punctuated but do not say which of the three speaks (the one who moved to Washington, D.C.). The record is the ROIR cassette ("known as the ROIR Sessions"). Formative-years fandom, so counted.

entries.speaker: interpol
entries.heard: I think he's one of the great songwriters, period. And he certainly had a big influence on me.
entries.quote: I think he's one of the great songwriters, period. And he certainly had a big influence on me.
entries.citation: A member of Interpol, on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, says of Aphex Twin: "He certainly had a big influence on me."
entries.note: The next caption line adds: "So it definitely changed the way I thought about music." Speaker not named.

entries.speaker: interpol
entries.heard: Alright, and then the last one was PJ Harvey's 'To Bring You My Love.' An artist I greatly admire and have admired for many, many years now.
entries.quote: Alright, and then the last one was PJ Harvey's To Bring You My Love. An artist I greatly admire and have admired for many, many years now.
entries.note: Admiration only.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.heard: I've gone for Sharon Van Etten, because I was in love. This is the only Sharon Van Etten album I haven't got yet, so it complete s my collection. I'm a massive fan, she's got such an incredible voice, writes beautiful songs.
entries.quote: I've gone for Sharon Van Etten, because I was in love. [...] I'm a massive fan.
entries.note: Album not named in the captions (the one missing from his collection). Fandom only.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.heard: and I bought the last few albums he's done, so this is just carrying on the habit. Not much more to say, I'm a big fan of Mac DeMarco
entries.quote: And I bought the last few albums he's done, so this is just carrying on the habit. Not much more to say. I'm a big fan of Mac DeMarco.
entries.note: Fan of recent records.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.heard: I picked up this, the new album by Godspeed You! Black Emperor. I love this band. I love the fact it's all instrumental. Massive sound. Nice, drone-y. Each song goes on for ages. I think there's a little bit of what we try and do in here as well.
entries.quote: I picked up this, the new album by Godspeed You! Black Emperor. I love this band. I love the fact it's all instrumental. Massive sound. Nice, drone-y. Each song goes on for ages. I think there's a little bit of what we try and do in here as well.
entries.note: Hears a resemblance to what Ride do; that is not influence. Heard text is the four caption lines the quote runs across.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.heard: I'm not the biggest Depeche Mode fan, but I thought that could be a good way to start.
entries.quote: I'm not the biggest Depeche Mode fan, but I thought that could be a good way to start.
entries.note: Buying it as a way in.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.heard: 'Another Green World' by Brian Eno. It's a good album but I bought it especially for the track 'The Big Ship'
entries.quote: "Another Green World" by Brian Eno. It's a good album, but I bought it especially for the track "The Big Ship."
entries.note: Praise only.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.heard: And one of my debuts on the decks was 'Victorialand' by Cocteau Twins. Now I didn't know the Cocteau Twins too well at that point but I put it on.
entries.quote: One of my debuts on the decks was "Victorialand" by Cocteau Twins. Now I didn't know the Cocteau Twins too well at that point.
entries.note: A record-shop anecdote; says he did not know them well then.

entries.quote: Caroline Polachek's Pang. A very cool record. I learned about her from her song "Breathless".
entries.note: Praise only.

entries.speaker: beabadoobee
entries.heard: which i unfortunately do not have one of their records yet but um yeah no they inspire a lot of my music
entries.quote: Which I unfortunately do not have one of their records yet, but, yeah, no, they inspire a lot of my music.
entries.citation: beabadoobee, on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, says of Dinosaur Jr. (with the Smashing Pumpkins, her two favourite bands): "They inspire a lot of my music."
entries.note: "They" is Dinosaur Jr. and the Smashing Pumpkins (she has just named both as favourite bands). Record is You're Living All Over Me.

entries.speaker: beabadoobee

entries.quote: He inspired me to kind of pretty much start music.
entries.citation: beabadoobee, on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, says of Elliott Smith: "He inspired me to kind of pretty much start music."

entries.speaker: beabadoobee

entries.quote: First record is Pavement, Slanted and Enchanted. I mean, I wrote a song about the guy, so it only makes sense.
entries.note: Praise; writing a song about Malkmus is a tribute, not a stated influence.

entries.speaker: beabadoobee
entries.heard: this next record is post by bjork um recently i've been like obsessed with this um
entries.quote: This next record is Post by Björk. Recently I've been like obsessed with this album.
entries.note: Recent obsession, nothing about her own music.

entries.speaker: beabadoobee
entries.heard: obviously i remember being in oxford with my band and just getting really into death tones
entries.quote: Obviously, I remember being in Oxford with my band and just getting really into Deftones.
entries.note: Borderline: got into them while in her band, but she does not say they shaped her music. Kept favourite to be strict.

entries.speaker: wilco
entries.heard: I got 'The First Four Years' of Black Flag. I really like this album a lot and I wanted to get it on vinyl. I love the first song 'Nervous Breakdown'
entries.quote: I got The First Four Years of Black Flag. I really like this album a lot and I wanted to get it on vinyl. I love the first song, "Nervous Breakdown".
entries.note: Praise; the captions do not say which of the three Tweedys speaks.

entries.speaker: the-smiths
entries.heard: First time I heard Wire, was when I was in school, I heard 'Outdoor Miner,' the single.
entries.quote: First time I heard Wire was when I was in school. I heard "Outdoor Miner," the single.
entries.note: Says he heard them at school and respects Colin Newman for never sticking to one sound, but never says it shaped his own playing. Kept favourite to be strict.
